SUMMARY

Article XIIIB (Proposition 4) of the California Constitution, as amended by Proposition
111, requires that local jurisdictions establish appropriation limits each fiscal year. This
limits the amount of revenue that can be appropriated in any fiscal year to the
Proceeds of Taxes. Proceeds of taxes include: all taxes levied by or for an agency;
any revenues from license fees, general use charges and user fees to the extent that
the proceeds exceed the cost of providing the service covered by the fee; and
discretionary State subventions. An increase over the prior year's limitation is allowed
in three instances:

1. Percentage change in California fourth quarter per capita personal income or the
  increase in the non-residential assessed valuation due to new construction.
2. Percentage change in the population of the jurisdiction or the county in which the
  jurisdiction is located, whichever is greater; and

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 061-2020 A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF HAWAIIAN GARDENS ESTABLISHING POLICY AND
  PROCEDURAL STANDARDS FOR CITY COUNCIL LEVEL GRIEVANCE
  PROCEEDINGS

SUMMARY

As part of the Memorandum of Understanding between the City and both the AFSCME
Management and Rank & File Bargaining Units, an employee(s) of the City or AFSCME
Representative(s) acting on behalf of an employee(s) of the City may file a grievance for "any
dispute, difference, or controversy related to wages, hours or working conditions ... ".

Depending on which bargaining unit the employee is a member of, a grievance may reach the
City Council level at Step 3 for an employee/member within the Management Bargaining Unit or
Step 4 for an employee/member within the Rank & File Bargaining Unit, if the matter is
unresolved at any of the previous steps of the Grievance and Arbitration Procedure.

Despite these requirements for grievances to be heard at the City Council level, the respective
Grievance and Arbitration Procedures lack specificity as to the structure and procedure in which
the grievances should be heard and presented before the City Council. Consequently, and as a
result of the number of grievances the City Council has recently heard, members of the City
Council have expressed a desire for staff to agendize this item to formerly develop and adopt
policy and procedural standards for City Council discussion that will provide some structure as
to how grievances at the City Council level are heard and presented while simultaneously
ensuring due process and maintaining decorum and etiquette throughout. It is the City
Council's discretion to develop and implement these policies and procedures to further ensure a
fair process by which the City Council impartially hears and makes determinations related to
grievances presented at their level.

DISCUSSION

In order to provide a more structured protocol in which grievances are heard by or presented to
the City Council during closed session, staff is presenting the following procedural standards to
be adopted and implemented moving forward by the City Council for their portion of hearing and
final disposition of grievances:
   P. 57
  •  The Mayor, or any designated Councilmember of his/her choosing, will preside over the
  matter and will be responsible for facilitating the proceedings and maintaining order
  throughout;

  •  AFSCME Representative(s) and/or Grievant(s) will be afforded fifteen (15) minutes to
  discuss and present its grievance to the City Council, unless extended further by the
  Mayor or designee presiding on his/her behalf;

  •  City Management Representative(s) will be afforded fifteen (15) minutes to present its
  response to the grievance, unless extended further by the Mayor or designee presiding
  on his/her behalf;

  •  AFSCME Representative(s) and/or Grievant(s) be afforded an additional ten (10)
  minutes for rebuttal or clarification questions from the City Council related to the
  information presented by City Management;

  •  City Management Representative(s) be afforded an additional ten (10) minutes for
  rebuttal or clarification questions from the City Council related to information presented
  by AFSCME and/or Grievant(s) representatives;

  •  Upon completion of rebuttals, the Mayor or designee presiding on his/her behalf, may
  open up the floor to the rest of the City Council for questions and/or clarification on
  matters related to the grievance to either party;

  •  Upon no further questions or clarification, the Mayor or designee presiding on his/her
  behalf will close the floor for questioning and dismiss all participants with the exception
  of the City Attorney and/or Human Resources Manager for deliberation;

  •  An official written response to the Grievant(s) will be provided by the City Attorney and/or
  Human Resources Manager on behalf of the City Council within seven (7) workdays in
  accordance with both the Management and Rank & File MOU's.

In addition to the stated grievance proceedings for consideration, the Mayor (or his/her
designee) at his/her discretion, may suspend the closed session discussions at any time for
improper etiquette, inappropriate/aggressive behavior, or for any misconduct being exhibited by
any of the proceeding's participants. Furthermore, the Mayor (or his/her designee) at his/her
discretion, may remove any participants who continuously exhibit any improper etiquette,
inappropriate/aggressive behavior, or misconduct, from the closed session proceedings.

In the event a grievance proceeding is suspended due to the behavior and/or conduct of any
participants other than the AFSCME Representative(s) and/or Grievant(s), the hearing shall be
scheduled to resume as soon as is practicable with all members of the City Council then
present. In the event an AFSCME Representative(s) and/or Grievant(s) is/are removed from
the proceeding or an originally-scheduled grievance proceeding is otherwise suspended due to
the behavior and/or conduct of the AFSCME Representative(s) and/or Grievant(s), the hearing
shall be scheduled to resume at the next regularly-scheduled City Council meeting (provided,
however, that if the AFSCME Representative(s) and/or Grievant(s) is removed or a proceeding
is thereafter suspended for an additional time(s) due to the behavior and/or conduct of the
AFSCME Representative(s) and/or Grievant(s), the City Council may proceed the completion of
the grievance process).

Lastly, per the MOU the City Council at their discretion, may elect to forego hearing a grievance
at their level for any reason and allow the grievance to continue to the next step of the
Grievance and Arbitration Procedure with an Independent Arbitrator from the American
Arbitration Association. Should this occur, AFSCME Representative(s) and Grievant(s) would
   P. 58
be notified accordingly of this decision in writing from either the City Attorney and/or Human
Resources Manager.

FISCAL IMPACT

None.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the City Council discuss proposed Resolution No. 061-2020 regarding policy
and procedural standards for grievances heard at the City Council level and provide staff with
direction for any necessary revisions. If significant revisions are necessary, staff will provide the
City Council with a revised resolution at its next regular meeting for adoption.

If the City Council is agreeable with what is being proposed without significant revisions, staff is
recommending that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 061-2020.
